answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to post a time-locked stake and earn reputation only through peer-attested work. Like basalt, the stake is hard to fake cheaply: one credible identity costs a deposit plus weeks of verifiable service. A flood of fakes would echo through the attestation graph, because new nodes with no shared history cluster and get quarantined. Each fake identity ripples cost outward, since the attacker must fund every stake, run every workload, and wait out every lockup, making a thousand-sybil attack pricier than any reward it could harvest.
